extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers, philosophers, educators, and advocates of free discussion and free speech
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical argument defending the necessity and benefits of free, open, and robust discussion for discovering truth, preserving the vitality of beliefs, and educating persons to hold convictions rationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full, frequent, and fearless discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: However true a received opinion may be, if it is not fully, frequently, and fearlessly discussed, it will be held as a dead dogma, not a living truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without open discussion truth becomes rote formula; active contestation keeps opinions alive and ensures they are understood, tested and justified rather than merely accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and be able to defend the grounds of one's opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the intellect and judgment of mankind ought to be cultivated... learning the grounds of one's own opinions. Whatever people believe... they ought to be able to defend against at least the common objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely assenting to an opinion without knowing its grounds is 'not knowing the truth.' Education should aim to give learners reasons and defenses, not only memorized conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hear opponents from those who truly believe them (strongest-form principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: He must be able to hear [opposing arguments] from persons who actually believe them; who defend them in earnest, and do their very utmost for them... in their most plausible and persuasive form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second‑hand or teacher‑framed refutations are insufficient; to properly test a view one must engage the opponent's case as its adherents would present and press it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in negative criticism and dialectics
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative criticism--that which points out weaknesses in theory or errors in practice--is a discipline indispensable as a means to attaining positive knowledge or conviction worthy the name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Socratic dialectic and disputation are valuable educational contrivances because they force learners to see both sides and thus attain real understanding; modern education should restore systematic training in this method.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no real opponents exist, imagine and supply them (devil's-advocate requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If opponents of all important truths do not exist, it is indispensable to imagine them, and supply them with the strongest arguments which the most skilful devil's advocate can conjure up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers and thinkers should create contrived difficulties and objections to keep the difficulties of a subject present to learners, preserving intellectual rigor even when genuine dissent is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of writing and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything must be free to be written and published without restraint. If teachers are to be cognisant of all that they ought to know, writings read by the instructed cannot be kept from the uninstructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricting publication or access prevents the necessary circulation of objections and replies; public access to controversial writings is essential for both teachers and the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief on authority is not genuine knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a class of persons who think it enough if a person assents undoubtingly to what they think true, though he has no knowledge whatever of the grounds of the opinion... This is not the way in which truth ought to be held by a rational being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting doctrines merely because they are taught by authority makes beliefs 'superstitions' or dead dogmas; rational persons should hold beliefs because they understand and can justify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion preserves the meaning and vitality of doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only the grounds of the opinion are forgotten in the absence of discussion, but too often the meaning of the opinion itself... Instead of a vivid conception and a living belief, there remain only a few phrases retained by rote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular contestation and explanation keep doctrines connected to their original meanings and practical implications; without it, doctrines atrophy into empty formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minority/dissenting opinions are valuable for completing partial truths
rubrics_metrics.description: When the conflicting doctrines... share the truth between them; and the nonconforming opinion is needed to supply the remainder of the truth, of which the received doctrine embodies only a part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpopular or heretical opinions often contain neglected elements of truth; encouraging minority voices helps correct one‑sided popular opinions and advances a more complete understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of opinion is inevitable but not unambiguously beneficial
rubrics_metrics.description: The cessation... of serious controversy, is one of the necessary incidents of the consolidation of opinion; a consolidation as salutary in the case of true opinions, as it is dangerous and noxious when the opinions are erroneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While widespread acceptance of true doctrines is desirable, the loss of the contestatory process is a serious drawback; societies should seek compensating practices to retain critical engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should present opposing arguments authentically, not only teacher-reconstructed replies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not enough that he should hear the arguments of adversaries from his own teachers, presented as they state them, and accompanied by what they offer as refutations. That is not the way to do justice to the arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogy must expose learners to genuine, forceful presentations of opposing views, so students can test and understand both sides rather than only rehearsed counterarguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical politics requires both opposing camps to be free and vigorous
rubrics_metrics.description: In politics... a party of order or stability, and a party of progress or reform, are both necessary elements of a healthy state of political life... Unless opinions favourable to democracy and to aristocracy... are expressed with equal freedom... there is no chance of both elements obtaining their due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public policy and political argument benefit from open contest between opposing positions because each corrects the excesses and deficiencies of the other; minorities often represent neglected interests that merit protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/educational contrivances (Socratic method, school disputations) are models to revive
rubrics_metrics.description: The Socratic dialectics... and the school disputations of the middle ages... were contrivances intended to make sure that the pupil understood his own opinion, and the opinion opposed to it, and could enforce the grounds of the one and confute those of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These historical methods, despite defects, provided intellectual discipline; modern education lacks equivalents and should adopt or invent similar practices to cultivate true understanding.
